quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive with your flashers on.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, you must pull over to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Stay calm and let it go.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut them off in return.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and let it go.
questions.explanation: Do not take road rage personally. If another driver cuts you off, stay calm and let it go. Continue driving safely.

questions.question: You are in an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help the injured.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop severe bleeding with direct pressure, but do not move injured people unnecessarily. Wait for emergency vehicles to arrive.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.explanation: A steady green arrow pointing down over a lane means you may use that lane.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: When weather changes suddenly, you must change how you drive.
Slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you during bad weather.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Always slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: Which is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place a baby or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can hurt a baby or small child, even in a low-speed crash.
Make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before you drive, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce the risk of injury or death in a crash. Children 12 and under must sit properly restrained in the back seat. Never put a rear-facing baby seat in the front seat of a vehicle with a front airbag.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing the radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Drivers make 200 decisions for every mile driven. You must focus completely on driving. Any other task can be dangerous and distracting.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Winding road.
Pedestrian crossing.
Low ground railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: This sign shows a low ground railroad crossing. The railroad tracks cross the road at a steep angle. The bottom of low vehicles may drag or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but hurts your judgment.
It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either one.
It has no effect on judgment but hurts driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms skills needed for safe driving, including reaction time and vision. It also affects your judgment of speed and distance, lowers your caution, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When school bus lights are flashing.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not pass if an oncoming vehicle is in the passing lane, if a curve or hill blocks your view, at an intersection, before or on a railroad crossing or bridge, or in any no passing zone. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road or a road with a center turn lane.

questions.question: Which of the following distracts drivers and increases crash risk?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.explanation: Cell phones (including hands-free phones) and audio devices like radios and CD players are dangerous distractions. They increase the risk of a crash.

questions.question: What causes "highway hypnosis"?

options.text: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
Frequent rest stops.
Too much sleep the night before your trip.
Short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare at the road ahead for too long and stop checking mirrors and blind spots. You can zone out and miss slowing or stopped traffic ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.
Right turns are not permitted.
Left turns are permitted.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: This sign is a regulatory sign that shows rules drivers must follow. Right turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What should a driver do after an accident?

options.text: Stop their vehicle at or near the scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: After an accident, stop at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand in traffic lanes—another car could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on an interstate?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder of the road if you are tired.
You should always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
You should change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing. Do not stop on the shoulder unless there is an emergency. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your freeway exit?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for an escort back to your exit.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit. Do not back up, stop on the highway, or cross the median to turn around. Do not swerve across multiple lanes at the last second. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: Are usually not important.
Are only found in construction zones.
Provide information for drivers.
Are usually red and blue in color.

questions.explanation: Highway markings give drivers important information. They help you position your vehicle correctly, show safe passing zones, and warn you about upcoming hazards.

questions.question: What should you do when making a left turn?

options.text: Proceed quickly, as you have the right-of-way.
Expect pedestrians to yield to you.
You have the right-of-way if the traffic signal is a flashing red light.
Yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.
questions.explanation: Yield to other drivers when turning left. Always yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic unless a sign, signal, flagger, or officer tells you otherwise.

questions.question: When are seat belts most effective?

options.text: The person driving the car.
Passengers when they are on a long drive.
All occupants of a car being driven on an expressway.
All occupants of a car every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: All occupants of a car every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in your vehicle should wear a seat belt every time you drive. In a crash, a person without a seat belt becomes a flying object and can hurt others in the car.

questions.question: How much lane space are motorcycles entitled to?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use the full lane width, just like all other vehicles.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: When changing lanes, check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.
Bicycles have the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be in the area ahead.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Get some coffee.
Open your window.
Stop driving.
Turn on the radio.

questions.explanation: Fatigue while driving is as dangerous as driving under the influence of alcohol. Stop driving if you feel tired.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through the intersection if no cars are coming.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on a steady red light if a sign does not prohibit it.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:

options.text: Loss of concentration.
Poor coordination.
Slower judgment.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol harms your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to pedestrians:

options.text: Only if the pedestrian is a child, elderly, or blind.
Only if the driver is not in a hurry.
Only when driving at night.
When the pedestrian is in a crosswalk at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pedestrian is in a crosswalk at an intersection.
questions.explanation: Slow down or stop at intersections to let pedestrians cross in marked or unmarked crosswalks. Watch for pedestrians who cross unexpectedly.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The combination can multiply the effects of both the alcohol and medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can multiply the effects of both the alcohol and medicine.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with other drugs increases how much both substances affect you. For example, one drink with a cold medicine can affect you as much as several drinks alone.

questions.question: If an approaching train is close or fast enough to be dangerous, you must:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait until the train completely passes before crossing.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the train completely passes before crossing.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is near or moving fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are broken.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the steering wheel and ask passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your vehicle unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your driver license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: When driving on major highways:

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to road hazards.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready for unexpected hazards. Avoid looking at one thing for more than a few seconds to prevent highway hypnosis.

questions.question: A stop sign is shaped like a(n):

options.text: Rectangle.
Square.
Circle.
Octagon.

questions.explanation: Stop signs have an octagon shape. This eight-sided shape means you must come to a complete stop.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must always be obeyed.
Are merely suggestions.
Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: You must always obey traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings. They control traffic flow and help keep drivers safe.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is a driver who:

options.text: Stares at objects off the roadway or daydreams while driving.
Maintains eye contact during a conversation with a passenger while driving.
Only watches the vehicle ahead of their vehicle.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Inattentive driving includes looking at passengers, daydreaming, or looking for things in your car. Keep your eyes on the road, check your mirrors regularly, and scan ahead to stay attentive.

questions.question: You are entering a crowded freeway. What should you do to merge into traffic?

options.text: Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the acceleration lane to adjust your speed to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up and match freeway traffic. Check your mirrors and blind spots. Yield to cars already on the freeway before merging.

questions.question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow the directions indicated by the traffic light.
Follow the directions given by the officer.
Honk at the officer.
Check to see what the cars next to them are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the officer.
questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, follow their directions instead of the traffic light.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Heavy traffic ahead.
Do not enter.
Railroad crossing.
Yield.

questions.explanation: This sign means it is not safe to enter the road or driveway from your direction. Turn around and find another way.

questions.question: The use of cell phones while driving:

options.text: Is not a problem in Idaho.
Distracts drivers and can cause crashes.
Is an uncommon occurrence.
Is highly recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Distracts drivers and can cause crashes.
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone while driving causes crashes. In Idaho, texting while driving is illegal. Hands-free devices are allowed.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road ahead curves right. Slow down to the safe speed indicated.
Divided highway begins. Slow down to the safe speed indicated.
Merge. Slow down to the safe speed indicated.
Winding road ahead. Slow down to the safe speed indicated.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right. Slow down to the safe speed indicated.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the road curves to the right ahead. Slow down to the speed shown on the sign (35 mph in this case).

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:

options.text: Are making a turn.
Have your emergency brake on.
Are changing lanes.
Are slowing down or stopping.

questions.explanation: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Keep them in working order.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Signal a lane change.
Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal before you change lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving.
